name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
description: SNAP provides monthly food benefits to help individuals and families buy healthy food.

other_requirements: Able-bodied adults aged 18 through 64 without dependents face a 3-month time limit unless they meet SNAP work requirements (ABAWD; upper age raised from 54 to 64 by the July 2025 federal law)
Resource limit applies in some cases

documents_required: Social Security numbers for all household members
renewal_cycle: Renewal packets sent 45 days before renewal due date; periodic reports required halfway through benefit period

benefit_schedule.description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotments for 48 States and D.C., FY 2026 (October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026)

name: Oregon Health Plan
description: Free or low-cost health insurance for Oregon residents who meet income limits.

other_requirements: Adults: 138% FPL
Children: 305% FPL
Pregnant: 190% FPL
Full OHP is available regardless of immigration status under Oregon's Healthier Oregon program (since July 2023) — includes undocumented residents and DACA recipients

name: Portland Mandatory Renter Relocation Assistance
description: Renters in Portland who are served a no-cause eviction or encounter triggering events may have the right to be paid relocation assistance from their landlord.

other_requirements: Landlord owns 2+ rental units in Portland
Rent increase >10% in 12 months OR no-cause termination
Tenant must demand payment in writing within 45 days

documents_required: Rent increase notice or termination notice
processing_time: Payment due within 45 days of demand
contact_org: City of Portland Rental Services Helpdesk

benefit_schedule.description: Relocation assistance amounts by rental unit size (one-time payment)

name: Employment Related Day Care (ERDC)
description: A child care subsidy program that helps families pay for child care and registration fees. Families may qualify if they are working, attending school, receiving cash assistance (TANF), on medical leave, or participating in certain Child Welfare programs.

other_requirements: Income limit to newly qualify is 200% FPL; already-enrolled families may stay eligible up to 250% FPL (exit limit)
ERDC may have an active waitlist due to limited funding — confirm current status

documents_required: Pay stubs or proof of income
contact_org: Department of Early Learning and Care (DELC)

benefit_schedule.description: Monthly copay amounts by family size and countable monthly income

name: Oregon Earned Income Tax Credit (EIC) and Oregon Kids Credit
description: Oregon offers two refundable tax credits: (1) the Oregon Earned Income Credit, which is 9% or 12% of the federal EITC depending on whether you have a dependent under age 3; and (2) the Oregon Kids Credit, a refundable credit for people with dependent children ages 0–5.

other_requirements: Must file Oregon state tax return
Kids' Credit: children under 6

name: Income-Qualified Bill Discount
description: A monthly bill discount program for qualifying residential PGE customers based on household size and combined annual gross income, providing ongoing discounts between 15% and 80% off energy use.

other_requirements: Income ceiling is 60% of Oregon State Median Income (SMI), adjusted for household size — NOT the federal poverty level. Discount tiers (15%-80%) scale by SMI band
Must be PGE customer
Account holder name match required

documents_required: Proof of income OR proof of enrollment in qualifying program (SNAP, OHP, etc.)

benefit_schedule.description: Monthly discount percentage by household size and annual gross income

name: Portland Water Bureau Financial Assistance
description: Financial assistance program provides bill discounts and other forms of assistance to income-qualified single-family residential customers for sewer, stormwater, and water bills.

other_requirements: Income ceiling is 60% of Oregon state median family income (~$52,128/yr for 1 person to ~$74,460/yr for 4); the HUD AMI 60% column is a close proxy. NOT the federal poverty level
Must be account holder OR have landlord verification

documents_required: Names of all household members and birthdates for anyone 60 and over
Total gross monthly income by source for all household members over 18
Accepted proof of income for all income listed in application
Pay stubs or earnings statements for wages
Benefit verification letter from Social Security Administration for Social Security benefits
Bank statement showing deposit or dividend statement for pensions, annuities, dividends, or interest
Court order for alimony or child support
Copy of check issued by agency or award letter for public assistance
Benefit letter for unemployment or veterans benefits
Profit/loss statement or dated lease for rental property
Benefit letter or court order for adoption assistance
Check or benefit letter for workers' compensation
Record with note indicating purchase for monthly payments from sale of property

name: NW Natural Bill Discount Program
description: An income-qualified bill discount program that can save customers money every month on their gas bill with discounts of 15% to 85% depending on state and income level.

other_requirements: Income ceiling is 60% of Oregon State Median Income (SMI), adjusted for household size — NOT the federal poverty level. Discount (15%-85% in Oregon) scales by SMI band
Must be NW Natural customer

benefit_schedule.description: Monthly bill discount percentage by household income level for Oregon and Washington

name: LIHEAP + Energy Trust Weatherization
description: OHCS provides funding to local community agencies that provide bill payment assistance programs. These programs assist low-income households to make their energy costs more affordable. They also help prevent the loss and the restoration of home energy service. Payments are made to the utility company on the customer's behalf.

other_requirements: Income ceiling is 60% of Oregon State Median Income (SMI), adjusted for household size (FFY2026: ~$38,384/yr for 1 person up to ~$73,816/yr for 4) — NOT the federal poverty level

name: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)
description: WIC serves lower-income pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants and children under age 5 who have health or nutrition risks.

other_requirements: Pregnant, postpartum, breastfeeding, OR child under 5

documents_required: Medical card for each family member

benefit_schedule.description: WIC cash-value benefit (CVB) for fruits and vegetables, maximum monthly allowances by participant category, FY 2024

name: Child Nutrition Programs Income Eligibility Guidelines
description: Annual adjustments to income eligibility guidelines used to determine eligibility for free and reduced price meals or free milk in school nutrition programs
legal_basis: Section 9 of the National School Lunch Act

name: Multnomah County Eviction Prevention and Energy Bill Assistance
description: Short Term Rent Assistance (STRA) is a unified countywide program that provides limited housing assistance to households in Multnomah County that are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. Also provides energy assistance to households with low incomes to supplement home heating and electric costs.

other_requirements: Income is NOT measured against the federal poverty level. Rent assistance (STRA) uses HUD Area Median Income (50%-80% AMI); the energy-assistance component uses 60% of Oregon State Median Income

documents_required: Eviction notice OR notice of non-payment

name: Community Energy Project Home Weatherization
description: Community Energy Project partners with low-income communities on the frontlines of climate change to create more resilient, efficient, and healthy homes.

other_requirements: Income ceiling is 50%-80% of HUD Area Median Income depending on the service — NOT the federal poverty level. The flagship free home repair/weatherization program also requires owning and occupying the home and being 55+ and/or having a disability

name: Senior and Disabled Property Tax Deferral
description: As a disabled or senior homeowner, you can borrow from the State of Oregon to pay your property taxes to the county. If you qualify for the program, Oregon Department of Revenue will pay your county property taxes on November 15 of each year.

other_requirements: Eligible if you are EITHER age 62+ OR have a qualifying disability (you do not need both)
Home must be primary residence
Net worth excluding the home must be under $500,000 (ORS 311.668)
Equity requirements apply

renewal_cycle: Every two years after initial approval

name: Portland Transportation Wallet: Access for All
description: A program offering free transportation resources (funds or credits) to eligible low-income Portlanders, helping pay for transit, e-bike and e-scooter-share, ride-share, taxi services, and more.

other_requirements: Access for All wallet requires referral by a participating community-based organization — not a self-service online application
Available once per calendar year

documents_required: Proof of income OR enrollment in qualifying program

name: Portland Inclusionary Housing Program
description: A program requiring that all residential buildings proposing 20 or more new units provide a percentage of the new units at rents or sale prices affordable to households at 80% of the median family income or below.

other_requirements: Units are restricted at 60% and 80% of HUD Median Family Income for the Portland MSA (FY2026: 80% MFI is $71,900/yr for 1 person up to $102,650/yr for 4) — NOT the federal poverty level
No central application portal: find IH units via the Portland Housing Bureau units list and apply directly to each building's own waitlist

name: SUN Community Schools
description: We ensure that the future is in good hands by making sure young people have access to a full range of opportunities throughout their childhood. SUN Community Schools offer after school programs, quality instruction, enrichment, and extra-curricular activities, links to food, shelter, and help with energy bills, connection to health and mental health services, and adult education and recreation.

other_requirements: Child must attend or live near a SUN school

name: Aging and Disability Resource Connection Helpline
description: The ADRC helps people of all ages, incomes and abilities learn about long-term support options and other programs and services in their communities.

other_requirements: The ADRC information & referral helpline is open to people of all ages, incomes, and abilities (including family caregivers); OAA-funded direct services (case management, in-home care, meals) prioritize adults 60+, adults with disabilities, and veterans

contact_org: Multnomah County Aging and Disability Resource Connection

name: Oregon Property Tax Exemption for Disabled Veterans
description: A property tax exemption program for disabled veterans and surviving spouses of veterans that exempts a portion of homestead property's assessed value from property taxes.

other_requirements: Service-connected disability rating, OR surviving spouse of veteran

documents_required: DD-214 or other military-issued documentation showing discharge/release under honorable conditions and period of active service
Certificate of disability (40% or more) issued by U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, branch of Armed Forces, or licensed physician
For surviving spouse/partner: marriage certificate or certificate of registered domestic partnership
For surviving spouse/partner: veteran's death certificate
renewal_cycle: Annual for physicians' certifications; not required for VA/Armed Forces certifications dated within three years or after age 65 with permanent disability certification

benefit_schedule.description: Property tax exemption amounts by disability/service status

amounts.condition: Disabled veteran certified by VA/Armed Forces with 40% or more disabilities, or veteran certified by licensed physician as 40% or more disabled (with income limit of 185% FPL), or active duty service members including National Guard and Reserve members

Veteran certified by VA/Armed Forces with service-connected disabilities of 40% or more, or surviving spouse/partner of veteran who died from service-connected injury/illness or received at least one year of maximum exemption

name: Lifeline
description: A federal program that offers a monthly benefit towards phone or internet services for eligible subscribers

other_requirements: OR enrolled in qualifying program (SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing, Veterans Pension, Tribal programs)

documents_required: Proof of income OR proof of enrollment in qualifying program

benefit_schedule.description: Monthly benefit amount by residential status
